title: The Isha Upanishad, with Shankara's commentary
attributionNote: Anonymous, and the last chapter of the Shukla Yajurveda; no author is claimed. The commentary beside the text is ascribed to Shankara.
description: Eighteen verses teach that the whole world is to be inhabited as the dwelling of the Lord, that the one who sees all beings in the self and the self in all beings is free of grief, and that knowledge and action, learning and birth are not enemies but are to be held together. It is the shortest and, for many readers, the most concentrated of the principal Upanishads.
historicalContext: Chanted as the closing chapter of the Shukla Yajurveda and quoted at the beginning of the Isa Upanishad's school commentaries, these verses became a standard text of Vedanta teaching and of modern Indian thought about action.
availabilityNote: Complete: all eighteen verses of the Kanva recension from the GRETIL e-text, streamed at read time, with the commentary ascribed to Shankara in a second pane.
